message.text:
q19.

REST via gRPC-Gateway — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go`
Connect (ConnectRPC) — `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go` and `server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go`

Both are wired up from the same `RegisterGateway` method. For the REST path, the generated gateway handler is registered directly against `APIV1Service` on a `runtime.ServeMux` that carries the auth middleware, and the mux is mounted on Echo under `/api/v1/*`:

```108:110:server/router/api/v1/v1.go
	if err := v1pb.RegisterMemoServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {
		return err
	}
```

For Connect, `ConnectServiceHandler` embeds `*APIV1Service` and registers the generated handler on an `http.ServeMux` (invoked at `v1.go` line 141):

```40:40:server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go
		wrap(apiv1connect.NewMemoServiceHandler(s, opts...)),
```

The per-RPC wrapping itself lives in `connect_services.go`, where each method unwraps `connect.Request` and delegates to the corresponding `APIV1Service` method — that's how a single business-logic implementation serves both protocols. There is no native gRPC listener in this codebase; no `grpc.NewServer` exists outside the generated code, so the two protocols are REST-over-gateway and Connect.
